thread:
Ivy: about to open a small docs PR that fixes region naming and adds a quick 'how to pick the right endpoint' blurb. want two reviewers for wording and an example snippet
Marcus: sounds good. can you add a short migration note for customers moving from global to residency-enabled accounts? Support sees confusion there.
Ivy: yes  i'll add a migration checklist: verify billing, set Data Residency flag, update SDK `base_url` or `region` setting, run smoke tests.
Tess: for SDK snippets, prefer showing the minimal change only. e.g. show this JS change rather than the whole quickstart:
```
// before (hosted)
const client = new Redwood({ region: 'us-west-2' })
// after (residency-enabled private)
const client = new Redwood({ base_url: 'https://private.example.com', timeout: 30000 })
```
Marcus: nice. also include the `X-Api-Version: 2026-01-01` header in curl examples and a one-line about expected 400 error when region is unsupported.
Compliance-bot: Suggested residency wording approved: "When Data Residency is enabled, processing occurs in the selected region; control-plane metadata may still be routed outside the region unless configured otherwise." Link: https://redwood.com/docs/compliance/data-residency
Ivy: added the wording and the migration checklist. i'll open PR and request @Marcus and @Tess. Posting link when created.
Docs-bot: PR created #2564 by Ivy: docs/region-endpoint-migration-note  reviewers requested: Marcus, Tess
Marcus: reviewing now  left an inline nit to make the migration checklist numbered so steps are copyable.
Tess: LGTM after nit addressed. will approve once CI preview is live.
Ivy: fixed, merging after CI. can someone sanity-check the private curl example in staging?
Marcus: i'll run the curl test tonight and paste results here.
Ivy: thanks everyone! :sparkles:
